ru.title: Восстановление исторических документов с помощью LLM и RAG
ru.desc: Исторические документы являются важными архивами знаний, но они часто трудны для чтения из-за физического износа. Существующие методы восстановления с использованием masked language modeling эффективно используют локальный контекст, но имеют сложности с восстановлением именованных сущностей, требующих внешних исторических знаний. Мы представляем новую структуру восстановления исторических документов, которая использует большие языковые модели с извлечением и генерированием (RAG). Наш подход значительно превосходит базовые методы и подтвержден экспертными оценками как полезный инструмент для анализа исторических записей.

en.title: Reviving History: Enhanced Restoration of Historical Documents
en.desc: This paper presents a new method for restoring historical documents that are often hard to read due to damage. The proposed framework uses large language models combined with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) to improve the restoration process. By integrating external historical knowledge, the model effectively restores named entities that traditional methods struggle with. Experiments show that this approach significantly outperforms existing techniques, making it a valuable tool for experts analyzing historical records.

papers.title: A Vocabulary for Multi-Agent Automated Research Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract  We introduce a vocabulary for automated research systems built from one or more agents to make their design choices easier to describe and compare. The vocabulary specifies 1) who the agents are, 2) what operations are available in the system, 3) who may invoke them, 4) how agents communicate, 5) what information is visible within and across runs, 6) how the next action is chosen, 7) how a run begins, and 8) how outputs are evaluated. A trajectory records one run from the input task to the returned artifact. Because agents, operations, and initialization may be stochastic, repeated runs on the same task induce a distribution over trajectories rather than a single behavior.   Our vocabulary turns structural design questions, such as when agents should communicate, gain or lose a capability, or carry information across runs, into testable choices. It also makes the evaluator a component of the system, since reported gains depend on how closely the proxy score matches true quality. That separation also splits the vague complaint that these systems lack taste into two failures with different solutions. Generative taste is the rate at which a system proposes novel trajectories before any score is observed, and evaluative taste is the gap between the proxy score and the quality it should match. We instantiate the vocabulary on recent autoresearch systems to illustrate that it covers designs that differ widely in structure.

ru.title: Словарь для автоматизации исследовательских систем
ru.desc: В данной статье представлен словарь для автоматизированных исследовательских систем, состоящих из одного или нескольких агентов. Он описывает, кто являются агенты, какие операции доступны в системе, как они взаимодействуют и как выбираются следующие действия. Словарь помогает формулировать структурные вопросы дизайна и превращает их в тестируемые выборы. Также он выделяет значение оценщика как компонента системы, подчеркивая связь между прокси-оценкой и истинным качеством.

en.title: Structuring Automated Research: A Vocabulary for Agent Design
en.desc: This paper presents a structured vocabulary for designing automated research systems that utilize one or more agents. It outlines key components such as agent roles, available operations, communication methods, and how actions are selected and evaluated. The framework allows for the exploration of design choices, particularly in how agents interact and share information across different runs. By distinguishing between generative and evaluative taste, the paper addresses common criticisms of these systems and provides a basis for improving their performance.

papers.title: TRACE: Business Rule-Grounded Reasoning Curriculum for Knowledge-Preserving Parametric Tool Retrieval in Enterprise LLMs
papers.abstract: Abstract  Parametric retrieval enables LLMs to retrieve tools implicitly by assigning each API a unique virtual token and training the model to generate it via constrained beam search. Toolsense shows that this regime has two critical drawbacks: it destroys parametric tool knowledge during training, and its beam-search decoding is too slow for real-time deployment. We introduce TRACE (Tool Retrieval via Augmented Chain-of-thought and Enterprise rules), a two-stage curriculum that resolves this dissociation. Stage 1 reuses the multi-format memorization SFT from ToolSense to seed tool knowledge with LoRA. Stage 2 is our core contribution: the model is trained to emit a thinking trace before producing a JSON list of tool tokens, using two data sources -- RRB pairs from ToolSense and queries synthesized to target business rules curated by domain experts -- both augmented with reasoning traces. This training objective preserves Stage 1 MCQ and QA probing accuracy while enabling single-beam greedy decoding at production latency. Evaluated on a combined enterprise catalog of 8,300+ tools across two enterprise product lines, TRACE training for Stage 2 not only preserves but improves tool understanding: MCQ accuracy gains +3.2 pp and QA probing gains +9 pp over Stage 1. On retrieval, TRACE achieves ~86% recall on Domain A and ~60% on Domain B -- compared to embedding baseline performance of ~27% & ~52% -- both with single-beam greedy decoding, making it directly deployable at production latency.

ru.title: TRACE: Новый подход к извлечению инструментов для LLM
ru.desc: Параметрический поиск позволяет LLM получать доступ к инструментам через уникальные виртуальные токены. Однако метод Toolsense имеет недостатки: он разрушает знания о инструментах во время тренировки и имеет медленный декодер. Мы представляем TRACE, метод, который включает два этапа и улучшает усвоение знаний о инструментах. В результате тренировки с TRACE улучшаются показатели точности и скорость извлечения инструментов.

en.title: Enhancing Tool Retrieval with TRACE
en.desc: This paper introduces TRACE, a method for improving tool retrieval in large language models (LLMs) by addressing the limitations of previous approaches. It consists of a two-stage training process that enhances the model's ability to generate tool tokens while maintaining accuracy. The first stage leverages existing tool knowledge, while the second stage incorporates reasoning traces to improve decision-making. TRACE demonstrates significant improvements in tool understanding and retrieval performance, making it suitable for real-time applications.

papers.title: Evidence Attribution in Visual Document Understanding without Coordinates or Region Labels
papers.abstract: Abstract  Reliable visual document understanding requires a model to attribute each answer to the evidence regions that support it. Recent benchmarks and systems express this step through a coordinate interface: the model outputs the coordinates of bounding boxes that mark the evidence regions in the document. Under this interface, vision-language models often fail to identify the right regions even when the answer is correct, a failure known as Attribution Hallucination. We present a study that investigates whether this failure is partially limited by what the model can express through coordinates. On a verified bilingual CiteVQA subset, we compare the coordinate interface with a language interface in which the model outputs only text, quoting its evidence verbatim, and a multimodal retriever returns the location of each quote as a page region proposed by a layout parser (tables and figures are quoted through their captions or notes); the comparison is repeated over six open vision-language models. Compared with the coordinate interface, evidence recall rises from at most 8 points to between 26 and 47 and the hallucination rate roughly halves, with little change in answer quality. Building on this comparison, we use the same quote-and-retrieve pipeline as a training scaffold: because region-level evidence labels are expensive to collect for long documents, we introduce a GRPO recipe whose reward is a judge's reading of the gold answer and crops of the retrieved regions, training the model to quote better evidence without any region labels and raising an 8B backbone's strict attributed accuracy from 22.4 to 33.8. These findings indicate a practical path to improve attribution"without a coordinate interface and without costly region-level supervision.

ru.title: Улучшение атрибуции без координатного интерфейса
ru.desc: В статье рассматривается проблема надежного понимания визуальных документов с помощью моделей, основанных на машинном обучении. Исследование показывает, что использование текстового интерфейса вместо координатного может значительно улучшить качество извлечения доказательных данных, снижая уровень ложных атрибуций, известный как Attribution Hallucination. Описанный метод позволяет модели лучше ссылаться на текстовые фрагменты, избегая зависимости от сложной разметки регионов. В результате, точность атрибуции повысилась, а необходимость в дорогой разметке документальных регионов снизилась.

en.title: Enhancing Document Understanding: From Coordinates to Quotes
en.desc: This paper addresses the challenge of reliable visual document understanding by focusing on how models attribute answers to supporting evidence regions. It highlights a problem called Attribution Hallucination, where models provide correct answers but fail to identify the correct evidence regions using a coordinate interface. The authors compare this approach with a language interface that quotes evidence directly, showing significant improvements in evidence recall and reduced hallucination rates. They propose a novel training method that enhances model performance without the need for expensive region-level labels, demonstrating a practical way to improve attribution in document understanding tasks.

papers.title: Characterizing Warp Divergence from Pascal to Blackwell
papers.abstract: Abstract  Since Volta introduced Independent Thread Scheduling (ITS), NVIDIA GPUs have been widely assumed to handle warp divergence in a fixed manner. We test this assumption across Ampere, Hopper, and datacenter and consumer Blackwell GPUs, using pre-ITS Pascal as a baseline. Combining cycle-accurate microbenchmarks, hardware counters, and static analysis of compiler-generated SASS, we separate stable behavior from architectural change. Across all tested generations, divergent paths serialize linearly with the number of paths k, following T(k) approx sk with no super-linear reconvergence penalty. Warp execution efficiency falls as 32/k, the penalty is independent of occupancy, and predication removes the serialization cost. The same behavior appears on Pascal, showing that this programmer-visible cost model predates ITS. The compiler-emitted reconvergence machinery, however, has changed substantially. Pascal uses a per-warp SSY/SYNC instruction stack, whereas later generations use barrier-register instructions. Deferred reconvergence beyond the immediate post-dominator falls from 29 cases on Ampere to 2 on Blackwell. Blackwell also introduces a two-tier convergence-barrier classification, uniform-branch instructions, and explicit partial-mask warp synchronization, none of which appear on Ampere or Hopper. Controlled bit-flip experiments indicate that the new barrier class is a static compiler classification with no observable runtime effect in our tests. Thus, divergence retains a stable and predictable performance cost even as NVIDIA's control-flow ISA and reconvergence mechanisms continue to evolve.

ru.title: Стабильность производительности при отклонении потоков в NVIDIA GPUs
ru.desc: В данной статье рассматривается поведение расчета в GPUs от NVIDIA с учетом независимого планирования потоков (ITS). Исследуются разные поколения графических процессоров, включая Ampere, Hopper и Blackwell. Авторы обнаружили, что поведение в случае отклонения потоков стабильно и предсказуемо, независимо от архитектурных изменений. Также были выявлены изменения в механизмах реконсолидации между поколениями, включая изменения в инструкциях и способах синхронизации.

en.title: Stable Performance Costs of Warp Divergence Across NVIDIA GPU Generations
en.desc: This paper investigates how NVIDIA GPUs manage warp divergence across different architectures, specifically Ampere, Hopper, and Blackwell, compared to the older Pascal architecture. The authors find that the performance cost of divergent paths remains stable and predictable, despite changes in the underlying hardware and compiler mechanisms. They demonstrate that the serialization of divergent paths is linear with the number of paths, and that newer architectures have introduced more sophisticated reconvergence techniques. Overall, the study reveals that while the control-flow instruction set architecture (ISA) has evolved, the fundamental performance implications of warp divergence have not changed significantly.

papers.title: UltraViT: Latency-Optimized On-device Vision Encoder for Large Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Abstract  Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) remain bottlenecked by massive computational footprints, precluding their deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. While efforts to compress LVLMs focus heavily on vision token reduction or smaller language models, the vision encoder is largely overlooked, typically deployed as a monolithic, computationally heavy feature extractor. Moreover, there is no previous effort that designs a vision encoder for LVLMs directly optimized for on-device latency. In this paper, we present UltraViT, a vision encoder for LVLMs, explicitly designed and optimized for on-device performance. Specifically, by taking into account real on-device latencies, we systematically design a pyramidal architecture that strategically integrates and adapts heterogeneous spatial mixers at the macro-block level. Furthermore, to pre-train UltraViT, we propose a novel two-stage generative pre-training strategy: cultivating rich spatial features via dense distillation, followed by direct generative supervision from a capacity-mixed frozen LLM. Compared to standard contrastive and SSL, we show that our pre-training is much more effective for achieving high-level semantic grounding for UltraViT needed for the subsequent generative multimodal alignment of LVLM training. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our on-device latency-informed design combined with our tailored training strategy establishes a new state-of-the-art for efficient LVLM encoding, significantly outperforming existing encoder-centric baselines while operating on-device at nearly 1.7xthe speed.

ru.title: Революция в кодировании для LVLM: эффективность на устройствах
ru.desc: В данной статье представлен UltraViT, новый кодировщик для больших моделей видения и языка (LVLM), оптимизированный для работы на устройствах с ограниченными ресурсами. UltraViT использует пирамидальную архитектуру, которая эффективно сочетает различные пространственные механизмы для повышения производительности. Также представлена новая стратегия предварительного обучения, которая включает плотную дистилляцию пространственных признаков и прямую генеративную супервайзинг. Эксперименты показывают, что UltraViT значительно превосходит существующие основы кодировщиков по эффективности и скорости работы на устройствах.

en.title: UltraViT: Optimizing Vision Encoders for Efficient LVLMs
en.desc: This paper introduces UltraViT, a vision encoder specifically designed for Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) to enhance on-device performance. Unlike traditional models that focus on reducing vision tokens or using smaller language models, UltraViT optimizes the vision encoder for lower latency on edge devices. The architecture employs a pyramidal design with heterogeneous spatial mixers, allowing for efficient feature extraction. Additionally, a novel two-stage generative pre-training strategy is proposed, which significantly improves semantic grounding and multimodal alignment during LVLM training.

papers.title: IndicTalk: A Large-Scale Persona-Based Multilingual Conversational Corpus for Indic Languages
papers.abstract: Abstract  Large Language Models (LLMs) have transformed conversational AI, yet high-quality multilingual code-mixed dialogue resources remain scarce, particularly for Indic languages where speakers naturally alternate between English and their native language in both native-script and Romanized forms. We present IndicTalk, one of the largest multilingual Indic code-mixed conversational corpora, comprising over 13,28,604 event-grounded multi-turn conversations across 18 language varieties covering 9 Indic languages. The corpus is generated through a fully automated pipeline that combines real-world news grounding, persona-conditioned dialogue generation using multilingual LLMs, and automatic quality validation. Extensive linguistic, automatic, and human evaluations demonstrate that IndicTalk produces fluent, coherent, and naturally code-mixed conversations across both script variants. We will release IndicTalk to support the development and evaluation of multilingual conversational AI for underrepresented Indic languages. The dataset is available at: https://huggingface.co/datasets/LingoIITGN/IndicTalk .

ru.title: IndicTalk: Корпус для мультиязычных разговоров на языках Индии
ru.desc: В данной статье представлена база данных IndicTalk, которая является одной из крупнейших многозначных разговорных корпус для языков Индии, смешивающих код. Она содержит более 1,3 миллиона многоповоротных разговоров на 9 индийских языках, где пользователи естественным образом переключаются между английским и своим родным языком. Корпус был создан с помощью автоматизированного процесса, который включает генерацию диалогов и оценку качества. IndicTalk поможет в развитии многозначного AI для недостаточно представленных индийских языков.

en.title: Empowering Conversational AI with IndicTalk
en.desc: This paper introduces IndicTalk, a large multilingual dataset designed for code-mixed conversations in Indic languages. It includes over 1.3 million multi-turn dialogues that reflect natural language use, combining both native-script and Romanized forms. The dataset is generated using an automated pipeline that incorporates real-world news and multilingual large language models for dialogue generation. IndicTalk aims to enhance the development of conversational AI for underrepresented Indic languages by providing a resource for training and evaluation.

papers.title: WorldDiT: A Unified Diffusion Architecture for World and Action Modeling
papers.abstract: Abstract  Many recent robot policies pursue stronger control by using large pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) as the action backbone. We introduce WorldDiT, a unified diffusion transformer architecture that couples action generation with visual world modeling and achieves strong performance without a large pretrained VLM action backbone. During training, a single diffusion transformer generates continuous action chunks and predicts normalized RGB patch targets from future camera frames. Across four LIBERO simulation suites, WorldDiT lies on the reported Pareto frontier for total model parameters and mean success among methods reporting all four suites. These results provide a strong sub-billion-parameter baseline for future scaling studies.

ru.title: Новый уровень управления для робототехники
ru.desc: В статье представлена архитектура WorldDiT, которая объединяет генерацию действий и моделирование визуального мира. Этот диффузионный трансформер позволяет добиться высокой производительности без использования большого предобученного VLM в качестве основы для действий. Во время обучения WorldDiT генерирует непрерывные действия и предсказывает целевые RGB-участки из будущих кадров камеры. Результаты показывают, что модель находится на границе Парето по количеству параметров и среднему успеху среди методов на четырех симуляционных комплексах LIBERO.

en.title: Efficient Action Generation with WorldDiT
en.desc: This paper presents WorldDiT, a novel diffusion transformer architecture that integrates action generation with visual world modeling. Unlike many existing robot policies that rely on large pretrained vision-language models, WorldDiT operates effectively without such dependencies. It generates continuous action sequences and predicts visual targets from future camera frames during training. The results demonstrate that WorldDiT achieves competitive performance while maintaining a smaller model size, setting a new baseline for future research in this area.

papers.title: DriveDNA: A Large-Scale Multimodal Naturalistic Driving Dataset and Benchmark for Driving Style Identification
papers.abstract: Abstract  Driving style captures stable, driver-specific patterns in how a vehicle is driven. In naturalistic data, however, this signal is hard to isolate because drivers are observed in different vehicles, on different roads, and under different conditions, so models may mistake vehicle- or situation-specific regularities for driver-specific style. We introduce DriveDNA, a large-scale naturalistic dataset and benchmark for personalized driving-style modeling, comprising 4,121 drives from 465 drivers across 115 vehicle models and totaling 975 hours of human-controlled driving at 10 Hz with forward video, collected from community drivers in everyday use. DriveDNA defines driving style as a consistent, driver-specific behavioral pattern in how a vehicle moves under similar conditions. The benchmark evaluates this signal through three core tasks: few-shot driver re-identification, personalized behavior prediction, and condition-matched comparison, and provides behavioral annotations plus 276,248 rule-generated maneuver events across six classes with large-scale human auditing. We evaluate baselines spanning classical descriptors, supervised and self-supervised time-series encoders, multimodal fusion, probabilistic prediction, and zero-shot foundation models under a fixed multi-seed protocol. Learned representations substantially outperform classical descriptors on unseen drivers (AUROC .935 vs. .707) and retain driver-specific information under matched driving conditions, while descriptor performance approaches chance. Video-only models achieve comparable re-identification accuracy but exhibit severe route leakage, showing that strong recognition may arise from contextual shortcuts rather than driving behavior. These findings show that reliable driving-style evaluation must assess both the behavioral value of learned representations and their robustness to vehicle, drive, and condition confounds.

ru.title: Новый взгляд на стиль вождения с DriveDNA
ru.desc: Статья представляет DriveDNA, новый набор данных и бенчмарк для моделирования стиля вождения, включающий 4,121 поездку от 465 водителей на 115 моделях автомобилей. Исследование подчеркивает трудности в выделении стиля вождения водителям из-за влияния различных условий. DriveDNA позволяет оценить стиль вождения через задачи, такие как повторная идентификация водителей и предсказание поведения. Результаты показывают, что обученные представления значительно превосходят традиционные дескрипторы в оценке стиля вождения.

en.title: DriveDNA: Unraveling Personalized Driving Styles
en.desc: This paper presents DriveDNA, a comprehensive dataset and benchmark designed to model personalized driving styles. It addresses the challenge of distinguishing driver-specific behaviors from vehicle and situational influences in naturalistic driving data. The benchmark includes tasks like few-shot driver re-identification and personalized behavior prediction, supported by extensive behavioral annotations. Results show that advanced learned representations significantly outperform traditional methods in recognizing driver-specific patterns while maintaining robustness against various driving conditions.
